1.title: Context Limits and Memory: Restart, Summarize or Persist
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Context Limits and Memory: Restart, Summarize or Persist. This module covers context limits and memory. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. What the context window is and why long chats degrade. The difference between length limits and usage limits. When to restart, summarize or persist. How memory, chat search and Projects carry context, and how to control them.

1.title: Case Check-In: Cedarbrook's Marathon Chat
1.text: Our running case is Cedarbrook Outfitters. Cedarbrook's Marathon Chat. A planner works on the holiday-season plan in one chat for three days. Early decisions get forgotten, the answers repeat themselves, and finally Claude warns that the message will exceed the length limit.

1.title: The Context Window
1.text: The Context Window. The context window is everything Claude can consider in one chat: your messages, its replies, uploaded files, tool results and instructions. It is finite. Length limit equals how long a single conversation can get. The newest models on paid plans support very large windows (up to about one million tokens; others five hundred thousand or two hundred thousand); part of the window is reserved for the reply.

1.title: The Context Window, continued
1.text: The Context Window, continued. Usage limit equals how much you can use Claude over time (a five-hour session limit and weekly limits on paid plans). The two are different: a short chat can hit a usage limit, and a long chat can hit a length limit. Automatic context management (with code execution on): when a chat nears the limit, Claude summarizes earlier messages so the chat can continue; your full history stays available. Longer chats still use more of your usage limit. What fills the window: long chats, large attachments, many tool results, and every connector's tool definitions.

1.title: The Context Window, continued
1.text: The Context Window, continued. Symptoms of a crowded context: forgotten early instructions, contradictions, repetition, slower and weaker answers, the error "Your message will exceed the length limit for this chat". Exam tip: A long chat that has drifted is fixed by managing the context (restart with a summary), not by repeating the same request or hoping for a bigger window.

1.title: Restart, Summarize or Persist
1.text: Restart, Summarize or Persist. The figure shows this: Restart when a chat has drifted or the topic changes, summarize to carry decisions forward, persist what you will need again in Projects, memory or saved documents.

1.title: Restart, Summarize or Persist, continued
1.text: Restart, Summarize or Persist, continued. Restart (new chat). Use when: The topic changes; the chat is very long, drifted or built on a wrong assumption; you hit a length limit. How: Open a new chat; paste only what is needed. Summarize. Use when: You want to keep decisions but shed the bulk. How: Ask Claude: "Summarize decisions, open questions and key facts so I can continue in a new chat"; check the summary, then paste it into the new chat.

1.title: Restart, Summarize or Persist, continued
1.text: Restart, Summarize or Persist, continued. Persist. Use when: You will need the same facts repeatedly. How: Put them in a Project (instructions and knowledge), memory, an artifact or a saved document; do not rely on one long thread. A handoff summary should list decisions made, constraints, definitions, open items and the next step. Review it: summaries can drop numbers and commitments. Persist the stable, summarize the changing. Brand voice and policy go in a Project; the state of today's task goes in a short summary. Starting fresh also cuts usage: a shorter chat costs less per message.

1.title: Restart, Summarize or Persist, continued
1.text: Restart, Summarize or Persist, continued. Editing an earlier message creates a separate branch, so you can try another direction without losing the first.

1.title: Memory and Chat Search
1.text: Memory and Chat Search. Memory. What it does: Claude stores useful facts as individual topics (role, projects, preferences, ongoing work) and uses them in later chats. Controls: On by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra; pause (stop using and creating), reset (delete all, cannot be undone), edit or delete topics in Settings, or ask Claude to forget something. Chat search (paid plans). What it does: Finds relevant past chats when you ask "What did we decide about X?". Controls: Turn off "Search and reference chats" in Settings.

1.title: Memory and Chat Search, continued
1.text: Memory and Chat Search, continued. Project memory. What it does: Each Project has its own memory, separate from other Projects. Controls: "Use account memory" off on the Project page fully separates it; deleted with the Project. Memory off for one chat. What it does: Start a chat without memory. Controls: Turn off Memory in the " plus " menu before the first message; it cannot be changed afterward; the chat stays in history.

1.title: Memory and Chat Search, continued
1.text: Memory and Chat Search, continued. Incognito chat. What it does: A temporary chat: not saved to history, not used for memory, not used for model training. Controls: Ghost icon; outside Projects only; kept for thirty days by default for safety even though hidden; cannot be reopened after closing.

1.title: Memory and Chat Search, continued
1.text: Memory and Chat Search, continued. The figure shows this: Layers of context: account instructions and memory apply broadly; Project instructions, knowledge and memory apply inside a Project; the chat holds today's work. What memory keeps: your role and projects, working preferences, people and places in your work, technical preferences. Sensitive topics (for example health, politics, religion) are off by default in memory. You can opt in; turning it off later removes saved sensitive items.

1.title: Memory and Chat Search, continued
1.text: Memory and Chat Search, continued. Never saved, even on request: government I D numbers, criminal history, financial account numbers, immigration status. Deleting a conversation does not delete the memories made from it. Delete the memory topic itself. Memory carries over; do not rely on it for facts you must always have. For must-have rules, put them in Project instructions (Module eleven). On Team and Enterprise, owners control whether memory is available but cannot read individual users' memories; turning memory off for the organization deletes everyone's memory. Import and export of memory from other assistants is possible but experimental; memory focuses on work-related topics.

1.title: Memory and Chat Search, continued
1.text: Memory and Chat Search, continued. In Projects, large knowledge uses R A G: Claude retrieves only the relevant parts, so a Project can hold up to about ten times more than fits in context (paid plans). Exam tip: "Persist" answers use Projects, memory or saved documents; "restart" answers apply when a thread has drifted or grown huge; "summarize" is the bridge between them. Incognito is for privacy from your own history, not for exemption from company policy. Exam tip: A new chat is not a failure: restart with a short summary when a thread has drifted, and keep stable facts in a Project.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Context window: Everything Claude considers in a chat; finite. Length versus usage: Length equals one conversation; usage equals over time (five-hour and weekly). Auto management: Older messages summarized near the limit; more usage. Restart: Topic change, drift, wrong assumption, very long chat. Summarize: Decisions, constraints, open items, next step; check it. Persist: Projects, memory, artifacts, saved documents. Memory: On by default (individual plans); pause, reset, edit, per-chat off. Project memory: Separate per Project. Incognito: Not saved, no memory, no training; outside Projects; kept thirty days. Sensitive topics: Off by default; some items never saved.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A planner's three-day chat now forgets early decisions and repeats itself. What is the best action? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Summarizing and restarting sheds the clutter while keeping the decisions.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team repeats the same twenty-page brand guide in every chat. What is the best way to persist it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Stable reference material that is needed repeatedly belongs in a Project's knowledge, not in a long chat that will be lost.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. What is the difference between a length limit and a usage limit? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Length is per conversation; usage is over time (five-hour and weekly limits on paid plans).

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An employee wants a one-off chat that is not saved to history or memory and not used for training. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Incognito chats are temporary, not saved to history or memory, and not used for training.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A user deletes a conversation that contained a personal detail Claude had saved as memory. What is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Deleting a chat does not delete the memories generated from it.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Select two. Which two belong in "persist" rather than in a chat? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. Reused reference material goes into a Project or saved document.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all six answers. Question one: D. Question two: C. Question three: C. Question four: B. Question five: C. Question six: A and C. In the next module, we continue the course.
